answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the garden index resolves every citation against the wharf checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the velvet audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 227 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 227 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 35 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
